text:
When I am dead, beloved,

Do not sing a sad song,

Nor pour gloomy cypress or fresh flowers

upon my grave.

Cover me with green grass

moistened by rain,

And if you wish, remember,

And if you wish, forget.

I shall no longer see the twilight,

nor feel the dew,

nor hear the song—sad as a lament—

of the nightingale.

Dreaming in a dusk,

neither dawn nor evening,

perhaps I may remember,

perhaps I may forget.




"Song"

translation.title: Funeral Song
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Rossetti's gentle permission to remember or forget after death.
